_note: All x_m/y_m are measured from the room's bottom-left wall corner (0,0), matching rectangle_segments(0, 0, boundary.x_m, boundary.y_m). OMX reference point intentionally omitted for now -- Step 1 only checks go-to-zone position/heading, no OMX-relative disambiguation yet.
_receiving_heading_note: Tried 180deg (9 o'clock) on 2026-09-02 to shrink GOTO_RECEIVING's large final-alignment correction turn (arrival heading consistently ~135-147deg, so a 0deg target needed ~135-145deg to correct, a large single turn_by_angle() call that measurably overshoots on this hardware -- confirmed a 176deg commanded turn landed ~32deg off, causing oscillation). Reverted the same day: `from_zone["heading_deg"]` also seeds the START heading drive_with_localization() assumes for the NEXT leg (goto_zone()'s start_pose) -- receiving->defect's path needs roughly -28deg initially (defect is down-and-right from receiving), which is close to 0deg but nearly opposite 180deg, so starting GOTO_DEFECT believing the robot faced 180deg sent pure-pursuit the wrong way entirely (dist_to_goal INCREASING run after run, confirmed on real hardware) -- a worse failure than the oscillation it was meant to fix. The large-correction-at-arrival problem is still open; a fix needs to target find_pose_via_map()'s turn execution itself (e.g. capping how large a single turn_by_angle() call it issues), not the zone's target heading, since changing that has this equal-and-opposite cost on the following leg's departure.
_exclude_deg_range_note: Optional per-zone [start_deg, end_deg] window (0deg = the direction the zone's reference scan was captured facing, +ve = counter-clockwise -- see common/scan_align.py's mask_from_angle_range()) excluded from scan matching at that zone. defect's OMX arm sits roughly -90deg (robot's right, facing 9 o'clock) from the robot and doesn't hold a fixed position between visits, so a wide margin around it is masked out -- matching relies only on the room's static wall geometry there. Widen/narrow/re-aim this if find_pose() at defect still shows elevated match_err, or re-derive it if the arm's physical placement changes.
_heading_tol_deg_note: Optional per-zone override for common/dock.py's REALIGN_TOL_DEG (default 3deg) used by goto_zone()'s heading-only realign_heading() stage. Raised to 10deg for defect (2026-09-01): even with exclude_deg_range masking, match_err there stays around 80-100mm (vs receiving's clean ~40-50mm), and chasing 3deg against that noise floor caused current~ to oscillate between roughly +10/-10deg for the full turn-step budget without ever settling. 10deg reliably exits that loop; tighten it if defect's match quality improves (e.g. once the OMX arm's positioning is more consistent).
_match_sanity_mm_note: Optional per-zone override (millimeters) for common/dock.py's SANITY_MATCH_ERR_M (default 120mm), used by find_pose()'s align=True path to decide whether to trust a position/heading estimate at all. Raised to 180 for defect (2026-09-01): a real, working partial correction there (8.6cm position error successfully driven down to 4.4cm) left the fit's residual stuck around 150mm on every subsequent scan -- confirmed not noise (many repeated stationary reads agreed closely) -- so the 120mm default was rejecting a legitimately trustworthy, still-actionable estimate every iteration and blocking the last bit of correction. Only used by align=True (find_pose()); realign_heading() (align_heading) doesn't use this gate.
